facts.claim: Negativity bias in digital feeds is a sequence involving attentional competition, moral appraisal and layered evaluation.
facts.quote: The findings of this study extend negativity bias from a final weighting effect to a sequence involving attentional competition, moral appraisal and layered evaluation.

facts.claim: Both semantic and response conflict were associated with mid-frontal theta-band and parietal alpha-band power modulations, irrespective of the level of conflict awareness.
facts.quote: We observed that both semantic as well as response conflict were associated with mid-frontal theta-band and parietal alpha-band power modulations, irrespective of the level of conflict awareness (high vs. low)

facts.claim: Stimulus prediction error was positively correlated with the power in the low-beta band (12-22 Hz) in the stop-locked interval.
facts.quote: Stimulus prediction error was positively correlated with the power in the low-beta band (12-22 Hz) in the stop-locked interval.

facts.claim: Individual differences on the inclination to mitigate, the sentence reduction per unit of judged sympathy, correlated with activity in the right middle insula.
facts.quote: Individual differences on the inclination to mitigate, the sentence reduction per unit of judged sympathy, correlated with activity in the right middle insula, an area known to represent interoception of visceral states.

facts.claim: Conflict detection is reflected in a DMPFC θ power increase that causally entrained DLPFC θ activity.
facts.quote: Subsequent conflict detection was reflected in a DMPFC θ power increase that causally entrained DLPFC θ activity (DMPFC to DLPFC).

facts.claim: Conflict resolution was completed by coupling of DLPFC γ power to DMPFC θ oscillations.
facts.quote: Conflict resolution was thereafter completed by coupling of DLPFC γ power to DMPFC θ oscillations.

research.angle: While the sources show that digital feeds involve moral appraisal and attentional competition, they focus on prefrontal cortex oscillations and visceral states rather than amygdala activation for survival threats.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that the brain uses specific prefrontal oscillations and visceral interoception to process conflict and moral appraisal, but it does not specifically link online outrage to amygdala-mediated survival threats.
research.caveat: None of the provided sources specifically measure amygdala activity or explicitly link digital conflict to biological survival threats.
